title: Air Chopper 7.5SC: which pack size should you buy?
description: Air Chopper 7.5SC is an insecticide for bed bugs, cockroaches and ants, sold in four pack sizes in Kenya. See how to choose the right size for the job.
answer: Air Chopper 7.5SC is a suspension concentrate insecticide used against bed bugs, cockroaches and ants in homes, hostels and small premises. It comes in a pack of three 15 ml units, 100 ml, 250 ml and 1 litre. Dilute it in water exactly as the label directs.
intro: Bed bugs bite at night, cockroaches work the kitchen after dark and ants follow any food left out. One product that treats all three saves you buying a different spray for each. Air Chopper 7.5SC is sold in four sizes, so the first decision is how much you need.

sections.heading: What does Air Chopper 7.5SC treat?
paragraphs: It is a suspension concentrate (SC) insecticide for bed bugs, cockroaches and ants. These pests thrive where there are cracks, crevices and warm, dark hiding places. Bed bugs shelter in mattress seams, bed frames and wall joints. Cockroaches settle in kitchens, drains and behind cupboards. Ants follow food and trails into rooms and stores.

sections.heading: Which pack size suits which job?
paragraphs: The range lets you match the size to the job: a smaller pack for a single home, a larger bottle for a hostel block. The pack of three 15 ml units is the smallest and the 1 litre bottle is the largest, with 100 ml and 250 ml in between.
How far each pack goes depends on the dilution printed on the label, so check it before you buy for a large space.

sections.heading: How do you use it?
paragraphs: Read the label first and prepare the dilution exactly as it directs. Spray cracks, crevices, bed frames, skirting boards and the other places where the pests hide or walk. Keep people, pets and food away from treated areas until the label says it is safe to return, and repeat the treatment if the label advises it. Before you start:
bullets: Wash bedding and vacuum mattresses, floors and corners
Remove food, and cover utensils and fish tanks
Treat all the affected rooms in the same visit so the pests do not move next door

sections.heading: What safety steps matter?
paragraphs: Wear gloves and a mask while mixing and spraying, and wash your hands afterwards. Keep the product away from children, pets, food and water. Never pour leftover mixture into drains, streams or ponds, and do not reuse the empty bottle. For a large or persistent infestation, call a licensed pest control operator. Store the bottle closed in a cool, dry, locked place.

faq: Which pests is Air Chopper 7.5SC used against?
Bed bugs, cockroaches and ants in homes, hostels and small premises.
How many pack sizes are there?
Four: a pack of three 15 ml units, 100 ml, 250 ml and 1 litre.
How much should I mix?
Follow the dilution and spraying instructions on the label of your pack. The rate is not worked out from the pack size.
closing: See the [[/p/air-chopper-7-5sc-insecticide-100-ml.html|Air Chopper 7.5SC product page]] for every size, browse [[/c/pest-control-fumigation.html|pest control and fumigation]], or read our [[/blog/how-to-get-rid-of-bed-bugs-kenya.html|bed bug guide]].

title: Bat CRP: getting bats out of a roof or hall in Kenya
description: Bat CRP is a heavy-duty bat repellent for roofs, ceilings and halls. See how it is applied, why sealing entry points matters and what safety gear to use.
answer: Bat CRP is a heavy-duty bat repellent chemical for roofs, ceilings, halls and other places where bats roost. You dilute it with water as the label directs and apply it where the bats settle. It comes in 250 ml, 500 ml and 1 litre packs.
intro: Bats in a roof leave droppings and urine that stain ceilings, cause strong smells and attract insects, and their noise at night can disturb families, guests and worshippers. Halls, churches, schools, hotels, offices and homes often need a way to move bats out.

sections.heading: What does Bat CRP do?
paragraphs: Bat CRP is a repellent, so its job is to make the roosting spots unwelcome. You dilute it with water as directed on the label and apply the mixture where bats settle, such as the underside of roofs, ceiling spaces, beams and corners.
Treat the roosting surfaces thoroughly and repeat if the label advises. The label also gives the dilution for roofing and hall areas, so confirm it on your pack before mixing.

sections.heading: What should you do before treating?
paragraphs: Prepare the area first:
bullets: Clear old droppings and wear protective gear, because dried droppings can create dust
Check local rules on handling bats if you are unsure
Plan how you will reach the roof, and use a ladder or platform safely

sections.heading: Why do the entry points matter?
paragraphs: Once the bats have left, close the entry points so they cannot return. Check the eaves, the gaps around the roof, vents and holes in walls, and seal them. Then clean up droppings safely and keep the roof space dry and clean. Regular inspections help you catch a new problem early.
Bats are useful animals outdoors because they eat insects, so the aim is to move them out of buildings.

sections.heading: What safety steps matter most?
paragraphs: Wear gloves, a mask, goggles and protective clothing when you mix and apply, and wash your hands afterwards. Keep the product away from food, water, pets and livestock, and out of reach of children. Do not let it reach streams or ponds. Store it in the original closed container in a cool, dry, locked place.

faq: Is Bat CRP a repellent or a poison?
It is sold as a heavy-duty bat repellent chemical. The aim is to move bats out of buildings, and the label has the directions.
How do I dilute it?
Dilute it with water as directed on the label. The label gives the dilution for roofing and hall areas.
What do I do after the bats have gone?
Close the entry points, clean up droppings safely and keep the roof space dry.
closing: See the [[/p/bat-crp-bat-repellent-250-ml.html|Bat CRP product page]] for the pack sizes, browse [[/c/pest-control-fumigation.html|pest control and fumigation]], or learn how to [[/blog/how-to-read-an-insecticide-label-kenya.html|read an insecticide label]].

title: Darvin 50EW 28 ml: a small pack for a bedsitter or rental
description: Darvin 50EW is an emulsion-in-water insecticide for bed bugs, cockroaches and ants. See why the 28 ml pack suits a bedsitter or rental unit in Kenya.
answer: Darvin 50EW is an insecticide for bed bugs, cockroaches and ants in homes and rentals. The small 28 ml pack is sized for a house, a bedsitter or a rental unit. It is an EW formulation, an emulsion in water, which you mix with water before spraying.
intro: A landlord or tenant treating one unit does not always want a large bottle. Darvin 50EW comes in a small 28 ml pack, which is easy to buy, store and use for a single treatment, and it covers three of the most common household pests.

sections.heading: What does EW mean?
paragraphs: EW stands for emulsion in water. It is a liquid concentrate that you mix with water before spraying, using the dilution printed on the label.
The pack is sized for a house, a bedsitter or a rental unit. How far it goes depends on that dilution, so check the label before you buy for a larger space.

sections.heading: Which pests does it treat?
paragraphs: Bed bugs hide in mattress seams, bed frames, headboards and cracks in walls, and they bite at night. Cockroaches shelter in kitchens, drains, cupboards and behind appliances, and they spread germs on food and surfaces. Ants follow food into kitchens, stores and bedrooms and nest in walls, floors and gardens.

sections.heading: How do you treat a rental unit?
paragraphs: Dilute exactly as directed on the label. Spray cracks, crevices, bed frames, skirting boards, door frames and other hiding places, and spray ant trails and entry points. Keep people, pets and food away until the spray has dried, and repeat the treatment if the label advises it.
bullets: Wash bedding at a high temperature and vacuum mattresses, floors and corners first
Treat all the affected rooms at the same time so pests do not move to rooms you have not sprayed
Check second-hand furniture and luggage for bed bugs before bringing them indoors

sections.heading: How do you stop the pests returning?
paragraphs: Store food in closed containers, wipe up crumbs and spills, keep rubbish bins covered, and seal cracks and gaps around pipes and doors.
Wear gloves and a mask when mixing and spraying, keep the product away from children, pets, food and water, and never pour leftovers into drains, streams or ponds.

faq: Is 28 ml enough for my house?
The pack is sized for a house, a bedsitter or a rental unit. How far it goes depends on the dilution on the label.
What pests does Darvin 50EW control?
Bed bugs, cockroaches and ants in homes and rentals.
Can I reuse the empty bottle?
No. Do not reuse the empty bottle, and keep unused product in the original closed bottle in a cool, dry, locked place.
closing: See the [[/p/darvin-50ew-insecticide-28-ml.html|Darvin 50EW product page]], browse [[/c/pest-control-fumigation.html|pest control and fumigation]], or read [[/blog/where-to-buy-bed-bug-killer-in-kenya.html|where to buy bed bug killer in Kenya]].

title: Fendona 60SC: a residual spray for hostels and hotels
description: Fendona 60SC is a BASF water-based alpha-cypermethrin insecticide with fast knockdown and a residual film. See how hostels, hotels and offices use it.
answer: Fendona 60SC is a BASF insecticide containing alpha-cypermethrin at 60 grams per litre, supplied as a water-based suspension concentrate. It gives fast knockdown and a lasting residual film on treated surfaces, and it is used for public health and household pest control.
intro: A hostel or hotel cannot treat one room and hope the pests stay put. Cockroaches, bed bugs, ants, houseflies and mosquitoes move between rooms, so the treatment needs to be planned across the whole building. Fendona 60SC is a 1 litre pack aimed at that kind of job.

sections.heading: How does a residual spray work?
paragraphs: A residual insecticide leaves a thin film on the surface after the water dries. Insects that walk across it pick up the active ingredient, so the treatment keeps working for a period after spraying. Because Fendona 60SC is water-based, it can be used on many surfaces in and around buildings.

sections.heading: Which pests does it control?
paragraphs: It is used against cockroaches, bed bugs, ants, houseflies, mosquitoes and other crawling and flying insects in homes, hostels, hotels, offices and food premises.

sections.heading: How do you treat a whole building?
paragraphs: Mix with clean water and apply as a coarse spray to cracks, crevices, skirting edges, behind furniture and other places where insects hide or walk. Shake the bottle well before measuring, because it is a suspension, and mix thoroughly in the sprayer. Rates can differ between markets, so always follow the rate printed on your pack.
Plan the treatment of the whole building in one go so that insects do not move between rooms.
bullets: Pay special attention to kitchens, store rooms, drains, door and window frames and bed frames
Keep a simple record of dates, areas treated and rates used
For large buildings or persistent infestations, consider a licensed pest control operator

sections.heading: What safety steps matter most?
paragraphs: Do not spray people, pets, food or cooking surfaces. Remove or cover food and utensils, keep children and animals out until surfaces are dry, and wear gloves and a mask. Fendona is very toxic to fish and aquatic life, so never rinse sprayers or empty containers into drains, streams or ponds. Store it in the original closed bottle in a cool, dry, locked place away from food.

faq: What is the active ingredient in Fendona 60SC?
Alpha-cypermethrin at 60 grams per litre, in a water-based suspension concentrate.
Is it safe near fish ponds and drains?
No. It is very toxic to fish and aquatic life, so never rinse equipment into drains, streams or ponds.
Why do I shake the bottle?
Because it is a suspension, shake the bottle well before measuring and mix thoroughly in the sprayer.
closing: See the [[/p/fendona-60sc-insecticide-1-litre.html|Fendona 60SC product page]], browse [[/c/pest-control-fumigation.html|pest control and fumigation]], or read about [[/blog/pest-control-products-for-hotels-and-restaurants-kenya.html|pest control for hotels and restaurants]].

title: K-Othrine WG 250: how a residual wall spray works
description: K-Othrine WG 250 is a deltamethrin water-dispersible granule in a 20 g sachet. See how a residual treatment works, where to spray and what to avoid.
answer: K-Othrine WG 250 is a water-dispersible granule containing deltamethrin at 250 grams per kilogram, sold as a 20 g sachet. It is a residual contact insecticide for walls and surfaces where insects rest, and the maker lists a residual life of 3 to 6 months on suitable surfaces.
intro: Spraying the air does little once the insects have settled. A residual treatment works differently: it leaves a film on the surfaces where insects land, so the wall itself keeps working after you have finished. K-Othrine WG 250, from Envu (formerly Bayer), is made for that.

sections.heading: How does a residual treatment work?
paragraphs: After you spray and the water dries, a thin film of insecticide stays on the surface. When insects land on it or walk across it, they pick up the active ingredient. Mosquitoes that rest on walls after feeding, including malaria-carrying species, are exposed when they land on a treated wall.

sections.heading: Which insects does it control?
paragraphs: It is used against mosquitoes, sand flies, houseflies, fleas, bed bugs and cockroaches in homes, hostels, hotels and public buildings.

sections.heading: Where and how do you spray?
paragraphs: Mix the granules into water in a compression sprayer and spray the surfaces evenly. Treat the places where insects rest, such as inner walls, eaves, ceilings and door and window frames. The amount per sachet differs for porous surfaces such as mud or concrete block and for non-porous surfaces, so follow the instructions on your pack.
bullets: Spray evenly, with a steady pace and a little overlap between passes
Do not wash or repaint treated surfaces soon after spraying
Keep a record of the dates and areas treated

sections.heading: What safety steps matter most?
paragraphs: Do not spray people, pets, food or cooking surfaces. Keep children and animals out until surfaces are dry, and wear gloves and a mask. It is very toxic to aquatic life, so never rinse sprayers or sachets into drains, streams or ponds. Keep the sachet closed in a cool, dry, locked place away from food.

faq: What is the active ingredient in K-Othrine WG 250?
Deltamethrin at 250 grams per kilogram, in a water-dispersible granule. It is made by Envu, formerly Bayer.
How long does the treatment last?
The maker lists a residual life of 3 to 6 months on suitable surfaces. Do not wash or repaint treated surfaces soon after spraying.
Why choose granules?
The small sachet is easy to carry and store, and the granules mix into water more easily than wettable powders.
closing: See the [[/p/k-othrine-wg-250-insecticide-20-g.html|K-Othrine WG 250 product page]], browse [[/c/pest-control-fumigation.html|pest control and fumigation]], or read our [[/blog/mosquito-control-at-home-kenya.html|mosquito control guide]].

title: Navigator 100 SC: cockroaches, bed bugs and mosquitoes
description: Navigator 100 SC is an alpha-cypermethrin insecticide for cockroaches and bed bugs, and a residual indoor spray against mosquitoes. See how it is used.
answer: Navigator 100 SC is a public health insecticide with alpha-cypermethrin at 100 grams per litre. It controls cockroaches and bed bugs and works as a residual indoor spray against mosquitoes. The dilution rate differs by pest and surface, so use the rate on the product label.
intro: Homes, hotels, hostels and schools often face more than one pest at a time. Navigator 100 SC comes in a 1 litre pack for repeat jobs, and a treated surface keeps working after it dries, so the result lasts beyond the day of spraying.

sections.heading: What is Navigator 100 SC?
paragraphs: It is a suspension concentrate (SC) containing alpha-cypermethrin, a pyrethroid that works on contact. It leaves a residual film, so insects that walk across or rest on treated surfaces are still affected. It is used for crack, crevice and surface treatments.

sections.heading: Where do you treat for each pest?
paragraphs: Cockroaches hide behind cookers and fridges, under sinks and along drains. Bed bugs live in mattress seams, bed frames and cracks near the bed. Mosquitoes rest on indoor walls after feeding, so for mosquitoes you treat the indoor resting surfaces as the label directs.

sections.heading: How do you prepare and apply it?
paragraphs: Read the label and measure the dilution for your target pest, because the rate differs by pest and surface. Do not guess it. Mix in clean water in a sprayer, shaking or stirring well, because this is a suspension concentrate. Keep people and pets out until the surfaces are dry, then ventilate the room.
bullets: Clean and declutter first, remove food, and cover utensils and fish tanks
Wash bedding and vacuum mattresses, floors and corners before treating bed bugs
Repeat treatment if the label advises it, because bed bugs often need a second visit

sections.heading: What safety steps matter most?
paragraphs: Check the PCPB registration number on the label and read the label before use. Keep the product locked out of reach of children. Wear gloves, a mask and protective clothing when mixing and spraying. Do not contaminate water sources, and do not pour leftover mixture into drains. For heavy infestations or large buildings, use a licensed pest control operator.

faq: What is Navigator 100 SC used for?
It controls cockroaches and bed bugs and is used as a residual indoor spray against mosquitoes.
What is the active ingredient?
Alpha-cypermethrin at 100 grams per litre, a pyrethroid, formulated as a suspension concentrate.
Will one treatment clear bed bugs?
Bed bugs often need a second visit, so repeat the treatment if the label advises it.
closing: See the [[/p/navigator-100-sc-insecticide-1-litre.html|Navigator 100 SC product page]], browse [[/c/pest-control-fumigation.html|pest control and fumigation]], or read how to [[/blog/how-to-get-rid-of-cockroaches-kenya.html|get rid of cockroaches]].

title: Promax 20EC: one concentrate for bed bugs, roaches and fleas
description: Promax 20EC is an odourless propoxur concentrate for bed bugs, cockroaches, fleas, ants and houseflies. See how one 1 litre bottle goes a long way.
answer: Promax 20EC is a propoxur-based, odourless insecticide concentrate for bed bugs (kunguni), cockroaches (mende), fleas, ants and houseflies. One 1 litre bottle makes 40 litres of ready-to-spray liquid, and it works with any hand-pump or knapsack sprayer.
intro: Bed bugs hide in mattress seams, bed frames and skirting boards, then bite while you sleep. A concentrate you dilute yourself means one bottle can cover a house, a hostel, a hotel room or an office, and you only mix what you need for the day.

sections.heading: What is Promax 20EC?
paragraphs: It is an emulsifiable concentrate (EC) with propoxur at 20% w/v, a carbamate insecticide that blocks nerve signal transmission and causes paralysis. It is odourless, which suits bedrooms and other indoor spaces, and it leaves residual action on treated surfaces so pests that crawl across later are still affected.

sections.heading: How much spray does one bottle make?
paragraphs: One 1 litre bottle makes 40 litres of ready-to-spray liquid. Most homes need only a small amount, so a concentrate goes a long way. The label gives the mixing amount for a hand sprayer, a garden sprayer and a knapsack, so confirm it on your pack before you mix. The knapsack amount is meant for hotels, hostels and large premises, while most homes need only a small volume of spray.

sections.heading: How do you treat bed bugs?
paragraphs: Half-fill the sprayer with clean water, add Promax, top up and shake well. Spray mattress seams, bed frames, headboards, skirting boards, cracks, behind sockets and furniture joints. Wet surfaces lightly; do not soak them.
Bed bug eggs can hatch later, so inspect after about two weeks and treat again if needed.

sections.heading: What safety steps matter?
paragraphs: Keep children, pets and fish tanks out of the room until surfaces are dry and the room is ventilated. Do not spray food, utensils or bedding you will use before it dries. Wear gloves, wash your hands after use and keep the bottle closed in a cool, dry, locked place away from food.

faq: What is the active ingredient in Promax 20EC?
Propoxur at 20% w/v, a carbamate insecticide in an emulsifiable concentrate formulation.
Which pests does it control?
Bed bugs, cockroaches, fleas, ants and houseflies in homes, hostels, hotels and offices.
When should I treat bed bugs again?
Eggs can hatch later, so inspect after about two weeks and treat again if needed.
closing: See the [[/p/promax-20ec-insecticide-1-litre.html|Promax 20EC product page]], browse [[/c/pest-control-fumigation.html|pest control and fumigation]], or read about [[/blog/odourless-bed-bug-spray-kenya-promax-20-ec.html|odourless bed bug spray]].

title: Tatua Demand 10CS: an indoor residual spray for mosquitoes
description: Tatua Demand 10CS is a capsule suspension insecticide used as a residual indoor spray against adult mosquitoes. See how the 25 ml sachet is used in Kenya.
answer: Tatua Demand 10CS is a capsule suspension public health insecticide, in Group 3A, used as a residual indoor spray against adult mosquitoes. It comes in a 25 ml sachet that suits homes, hostels, small hotels and offices. Dilute and apply it as the label directs.
intro: Mosquitoes rest on walls and ceilings after feeding. A residual spray leaves a protective layer on those surfaces, so mosquitoes that land there are killed over a period of time. Tatua Demand 10CS is made for that indoor job.

sections.heading: What does capsule suspension mean?
paragraphs: CS stands for capsule suspension, a formulation that holds the active ingredient in tiny capsules. This helps it stay on surfaces longer. It is a practical tool for homes in areas where mosquitoes are a problem, particularly alongside other protection such as treated nets and screens.

sections.heading: How do you apply it?
paragraphs: Spray the walls and ceilings as directed by the label, using the dilution printed there. Remove or cover food, utensils and fish tanks before treating, and keep people and pets out of the room until the spray is dry. The 25 ml sachet is easy to store and handle, and it suits homes, hostels, small hotels and offices.

sections.heading: How can you reduce mosquito breeding?
paragraphs: Fewer mosquitoes arriving means less work for the spray. Take these steps around the home:
bullets: Empty standing water from buckets, tins, tyres and flower pots
Clean gutters and cover water tanks
Use treated bed nets and window screens for extra protection

sections.heading: What safety steps matter?
paragraphs: Keep the product away from children, food and pets and read the label before use. Check the PCPB registration number on the label. Wear gloves and a mask when mixing and spraying, and do not contaminate water sources. Keep the sachet in a cool, dry, locked place, away from food.

faq: Is Tatua Demand 10CS suitable for indoor use?
It is a public health insecticide used as an indoor residual spray against mosquitoes, as directed on the label.
What does 10CS mean?
CS stands for capsule suspension, a formulation that holds the active ingredient in tiny capsules so that it stays on surfaces longer.
How much do I mix?
Follow the dilution on the label of your sachet.
Can I pay by M-Pesa?
Yes. Pay by M-Pesa and we deliver to all 47 counties, or you can pick up at The Sarit Centre, Westlands, Nairobi.
closing: See the [[/p/tatua-demand-10cs-insecticide-25-ml.html|Tatua Demand 10CS product page]], browse [[/c/pest-control-fumigation.html|pest control and fumigation]], or read our [[/blog/mosquito-control-at-home-kenya.html|mosquito control guide]].
